knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Surface Integral Using Stokes' Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle - \cos{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 1\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle 3 y, - 3 x, 0\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle 3 y, - 3 x, 0\rangle \\ & =\langle 3 \left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), - 3 \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), 0\rangle \\ & =\langle - 9 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - 9 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\cdot \langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(- 9 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(- 9 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 9 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =- 9 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 9 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(-9\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- 9 t\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(- 18 \pi\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right) \\ & =- 18 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, - \sin{\left(t \right)}, 3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle 2 y - 2 z, - 2 x + 2 z, 2 x - 2 y\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle 2 y - 2 z, - 2 x + 2 z, 2 x - 2 y\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) - 2 \left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3\right), - 2 \left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) + 2 \left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3\right), 2 \left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) - 2 \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 6 - 8 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 6 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 6, 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - \cos{\left(t \right)}, 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 6 - 8 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 6 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 6, 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle\cdot \langle 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - \cos{\left(t \right)}, 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle \\ & =\left(6 - 8 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(6 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 6\right)\cdot \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ & =\left(- 16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 12 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(6 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 12 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ & =- 16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 12 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 16 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(t \right)} \\ & =12 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(12 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 16\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- 16 t\right) + \left(6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(- 12 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(- 32 \pi\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(-12\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(-12\right)\right) \\ & =- 32 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle - 2 t^{2} + 2 t, t^{3} - t^{2}, - 3 t^{2} + 3 t\rangle$ for $t\in [0,1).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle 4 z, 0, 6 y\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- 2 t^{2} + 2 t,\quad y=t^{3} - t^{2},\quad z=- 3 t^{2} + 3 t
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle 4 z, 0, 6 y\rangle \\ & =\langle 4 \left(- 3 t^{2} + 3 t\right), 0, 6 \left(t^{3} - t^{2}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 12 t^{2} + 12 t, 0, 6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 t^{2} + 2 t\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(t^{3} - t^{2}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 3 t^{2} + 3 t\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 - 4 t, 3 t^{2} - 2 t, 3 - 6 t\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - 12 t^{2} + 12 t, 0, 6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\rangle\cdot \langle 2 - 4 t, 3 t^{2} - 2 t, 3 - 6 t\rangle \\ & =\left(- 12 t^{2} + 12 t\right)\cdot \left(2 - 4 t\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2} - 2 t\right)+\left(6 t^{3} - 6 t^{2}\right)\cdot \left(3 - 6 t\right) \\ & =\left(48 t^{3} - 72 t^{2} + 24 t\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(- 36 t^{4} + 54 t^{3} - 18 t^{2}\right) \\ & =- 36 t^{4} + 102 t^{3} - 90 t^{2} + 24 t \\ & =- 36 t^{4} + 102 t^{3} - 90 t^{2} + 24 t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{1} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{1}\left(- 36 t^{4} + 102 t^{3} - 90 t^{2} + 24 t\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- 30 t^{3}\right) + \left(- \frac{36 t^{5}}{5}\right) + \left(12 t^{2}\right) + \left(\frac{51 t^{4}}{2}\right)\right]_{0}^{1} \\ & =\left(\left(-30\right) + \left(- \frac{36}{5}\right) + \left(12\right) + \left(\frac{51}{2}\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right)\right) \\ & =\frac{3}{10}\end{aligned}
$$
